current_activity: Corps command post at Vouziers, France; the corps is to prepare to occupy Trier, Koblenz and the Saar-Palatinate
notes: Event date: 28 March 1945 (History of the Fifteenth US Army, printed pp. 90-91 and 92-93: Letters of Instructions Numbers Thirteen and Fourteen, both dated 28 March 1945, list the corps command post in paragraph 5; Number Fourteen reads 'XXIII Corps - Present: VOUZIERS - Final: To be Reported'). Event definition: a command-post observation from the army's own orders, not a move; the corps (APO 103) is to 'continue present mission' (Number Thirteen) and 'be prepared to occupy, organize and govern' Regierungsbezirke Trier and Koblenz, the Saarland, the Palatinate and the part of Hessen west of the Rhine (Number Fourteen). Relationship: Fifteenth Army assigned from 21 January 1945 (Wikipedia, Fifteenth Army, 'Subordinate units': XXIII Corps 21 January 1945 to 31 January 1946; TheSecondWar.pl: the corps 'was assigned' to the army on 21 January 1945); the start date comes from these two secondary accounts and no primary source read states it, while the army's orders of 28 March address the corps as a subordinate. Location: Vouziers, Ardennes (grid T8094 in the letters); the town centre stands for the command post and the grid reference was not plotted. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Vouziers. Commander: Maj. Gen. Hugh J. Gaffey from 17 March 1945 (Wikipedia, XXIII Corps, 'Commanders'; TheSecondWar.pl: 'from 17 March' after Maj. Gen. James A. Van Fleet; The Supreme Command, appendix D, p. 540, lists Van Fleet and then Gaffey without dates). Search: no source read places the corps headquarters at any date before this letter: TheSecondWar.pl gives 12 October 1944 as its arrival in the theatre, warns that the date should be treated with caution, and says only that the headquarters was in Britain in autumn 1944 and began operating on the Continent in January 1945, with no place named; no claim is made for those months. Event support: moderate (two letters of one date in one official history). Location support: moderate (named town in the army's order on the date; no second source for the place).
